gallery.title: File:Woodlands Trace - Snow on the Great Western Iron Furnace - NARA - 7722897.jpg
gallery.credit: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
gallery.source: Woodlands Trace - Snow on the Great Western Iron Furnace
gallery.description:
Scope and content:  The original finding aid described this photograph as:
Original Caption: Snow outlines every block of the Great Western Furnace, which stands as one of the few remaining remnants of the area's former iron industry.
Location: Kentucky (36.641° N 87.976° W)
Status: Public domain. Photograph by Sherry Bailey
The sign in the foreground reads:

3C 31
GREAT WESTERN FURNACE
Built in 1854 by Brian, Newell & Co., this steam cold-blast charcoal furnace was built of limestone from the surrounding hills.  Brown iron-ore came from shallow deposits about two miles north.  Pig-iron was shipped by river or hauled to rolling mills to the east.  It closed in 1856, due to lack of ore and to a slave insurrection by the furnace crew.

gallery.title: File:LBL Wildfire Feb 28, 2016 (26296090715).jpg
gallery.artist: Land Between the Lakes KY/TN from Golden Pond, KY, USA
gallery.description: The wildfire that started early afternoon on Sunday, February 28, at Land Between The Lakes. The 911 call came in around 3pm directing emergency personnel to the forested area off Forest Service Road 120 in Lyon County, Ky. The U.S. Forest Service dispatched two fire engines along with available firefighters. Eddyville and Kuttawa firefighters also responded to the call. Working together, firefighters built a fire break which contained the wildfire to 43.8 acres using natural features and hand tools. The fire is currently 28.8 acres in size, with the interior showing minimal activity. The larger containment area allowed us to minimize impacts to cultural and natural resources.  Staff photo

gallery.title: File:Fort Henry Site.jpg
gallery.description: View of the site of Fort Henry in Tennessee. Fort Henry was built in 1861 by the Confederate Army and would be controlled by the CSA until surrendering after the Battle of Fort Henry. The site was submerged with the creation of the Kentucky Dam and Kentucky Lake between 1938 and 1944. The site is a part of and accessible from Land Between the Lakes NRA. The site was added to the NRHP in 1975.
